decision: Treat the issue as needing full anchor, alias and merge-key support, because on main any file with an anchor fails to load (exit 4) and the reported bug cannot happen there
reason: Anchors and aliases aren't supported, so the reporter's file fails to load with exit 4. The fix has to add anchor support with the contract's rules from the start

decision: An alias is the anchored Node object itself, and the alias is recorded on the Entry or Item that holds it
options: Shared node object recorded on entry/item
Separate AliasNode type pointing at its target
reason: With an AliasNode, every consumer (to_data, render, leaves, sources, plan, apply, _matches) would need a new case. The shared object reads correctly unchanged

decision: A node's span excludes its anchor and any properties after it, so replacing the value keeps the &name
reason: Every edit primitive takes node.start as the start of the value's own text. A span that included &name would make a replace remove the anchor

decision: A later anchor with the same name replaces the earlier one. An undefined alias, or an alias inside its own anchor, fails to load. Anchored or alias keys stay refused
Add the scenario that an alias inside the node it refers to fails to load with exit 4, and treat an include string as not a mapping for a merge-key value
reason: Recursive alias should also fail to load

decision: Memoise the loader's expand by node identity, so an anchored node or include is expanded once and shared by all its aliases
reason: Without the memo, the second visit would see an already-replaced entry.value and include the file again as a separate tree

decision: overrides.merge carries the alias marker from either the base entry or the override onto merged entries
reason: A write below either side would go through it. Otherwise the alias marker is lost in mapping-form includes

decision: Honour merge keys (<<) when reading: the builder resolves them, and the mapping as written is kept in `written`
options: Treat << as an ordinary key (YAML 1.2 core)
reason: People who write `<<: *base` mean a merge, and get should answer accordingly

decision: Merge order: the mapping's own keys win, then earlier sources in the list. Merged entries take the << entry's position
reason: Follows the YAML merge-key spec

decision: Anchors and aliases do not cross files
A value supplied by a merge key cannot be set, even with --expand-alias (exit 3)
options: Write a local key that shadows the merged value
reason: Merges are shallow: a local mapping would silently replace every merged sub-key, and a local scalar would silently shadow the anchor. Refusing can be relaxed later

decision: Deleting or replacing anything that holds a << entry is refused
reason: 'Never written' covers removal, and the user can still do it by hand

decision: Write a new key named << quoted ('<<'), so it is never a merge key
reason: Written plain, it would read back as a merge key

decision: The planner raises typed refusals, the WriteRefused subclasses ThroughAlias and MergeKeyWrite, and the alias and merge checks live in one place in the planner
reason: One place decides whether a write goes through an alias, and one decides whether it touches a merge key

decision: Implement --expand-alias as a retry loop in compute_set: expand the alias the planner stopped at, reload and plan again
options: Separate expansion pass that pre-computes every alias on PATH and in VALUE's diff
reason: A pre-pass would duplicate the planner's walk. The retry reuses the one place that knows when a write crosses an alias

decision: The copy is the anchored node as written (quoting, number formats, include strings and nested aliases kept), rendered in block style without anchors or comments
options: Render from the resolved data with render_value
reason: Rendering resolved data would silently turn nested aliases into copies, replace include strings with their content and change quoting and number formats. An anchor in the copy would re-bind later aliases

decision: A multi-line scalar in the copy is rendered by render_value, and an empty collection becomes {} or []
A copy that would contain a << entry is refused with MergeKeyWrite
reason: Merge keys are never written

decision: --expand-alias expands every alias the set would otherwise be refused for, including nested ones and those a mapping or list VALUE reaches into
options: Expand every alias in the way
reason: Expanding only the first would leave the command refused even though the flag asks for expansion

decision: With no alias in the way, --expand-alias has no effect
reason: Re-running a command after the expansion succeeds instead of failing, the same reasoning as --in-include

decision: An existing end-of-line comment on the alias line is kept, and the marker goes after it with two spaces
reason: Losing a user's comment is not allowed, and the marker still ends the key's line

decision: An alias inside a flow collection is not expanded and the set exits 3
reason: A block-style copy cannot go inside {…} or […]

decision: A path through an alias in an included file, or in the included layer of a mapping-form include, is refused even when an override would be written elsewhere
reason: It refuses more than strictly needed, but it can never write through an anchor

decision: Setting the alias path itself, a new key below an alias, or a mapping VALUE that reaches into an alias is refused. Removing an entry whose value is an alias is allowed
reason: Removing an alias entry changes nothing else

decision: A VALUE equal to the current value is a no-op before any refusal, so no alias is expanded
Deleting an anchored node that is still used is not special-cased. The reload fails and _reload turns that into exit 3
Slot.indicator_end moves past the node's anchor when the anchor is on the same line, so text inserted after the indicator keeps the anchor
reason: The single place that decides it

decision: --expand-alias is a store_true flag on set that is passed to compute_set. plan does not take it
reason: The decision lives in the D4 loop

decision: An event is recorded for every path whose value changed, including alias and merge paths, all in one change. An expansion alone records nothing
Build the read-back check's expected value by node identity (apply._expected) instead of from plain data
reason: The old check expected only PATH to change and refused every set at an anchor, because the aliases change too

decision: Measure an alias entry's extent by its *name text (held_span/held_end)
reason: Deleting an alias entry, appending after one, and owned_end all measured the anchored node elsewhere in the file. Deleting settings: *d produced a duplicate key

decision: VALUE still cannot contain anchors or aliases (exit 2), now checked in values.parse_value
reason: The loader no longer refuses them, and writing anchors in new values is a non-goal

decision: An anchored empty scalar starts at its anchor's end, not on the next line
reason: after_anchor skipped the line break into the next key

decision: The ThroughAlias message names the equivalent path at the anchor (e.g. defaults.model), not only the anchor
options: Name the equivalent path at the anchor
reason: The hint should name the equivalent path at the anchor

decision: Lists are diffed by position, so setting a list whose changed item is an alias is refused
reason: [2] would change item 0, which is the alias

decision: New keys in a mapping with << go after its last written entry, not after merged-in entries
reason: Merged-in entries live at the anchor

decision: Accept that setting coder.<< on a merging mapping is refused with a duplicate-key message instead of the merge-key one
reason: It is still exit 3 with no file changed

decision: An anchored include string that gets a key added through expansion becomes a mapping-form include ($ref) in the copy
Replace test_anchors_are_refused_at_load with new per-feature test files (loading, anchors, through-alias, merge keys, expand-alias) and an end-to-end smoke test of the issue's file
Check test strength by breaking the code (disable the alias check, drop the merge alias carry, ignore `written`) and confirming the tests fail
reason: To confirm the tests catch regressions

decision: Reword two tasks' verify steps to name the tests that actually depend on the code
reason: Some of the tests they named don't depend on the code in question

decision: Commit the planning artifacts before implementing, then commit in small per-group commits on main with no push or PR
Fix the ruff failure in a follow-up commit instead of amending the commit that failed
Archive the change as task 6.3 and append implementation notes to the archived design.md
reason: The previous archive commit added implementation notes, and some things differ from the plan

decision: Leave issue #2 open, with no comment, and ask the owner
Replace README decision 8 and add decisions 39–47 for the points the contract leaves open
